question.text: If $\sin ^{-1}\left(x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{4}-\frac{x^{4}}{8}+\ldots\right)=\frac{\pi}{6},$ where $|x|    < 2$ then the value of $x$ is

solution.text:
We have, $\sin ^{-1}\left(x-\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{4}-\frac{x^{4}}{8}+\ldots\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$
$\Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{1-\left(\frac{-x}{2}\right)}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6} \quad\left[\because S_{\infty}=\frac{a}{1-r}\right]$
$\Rightarrow \quad \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{2+x}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{2 x}{2+x}=\sin \frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow \frac{2 x}{2+x}=\frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \quad 4 x=2+x \quad \Rightarrow \quad 3 x=2 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{2}{3}$
